part.text:
## Answer

**Yes — the option was renamed from `FIRST` to `RANK`.**

LPOS was first added under the temporary name `LRANK` (commit `a7936ef96`, "LRANK: Add command (the command will be renamed LPOS)"), then implemented as `LPOS` with an option token of `FIRST`. The token was subsequently renamed to `RANK`, and that option name is what the current tree uses (`src/commands/lpos.json` line 66: `"token": "RANK"`; `src/t_list.c` line 970: `if (!strcasecmp(opt,"RANK") && moreargs)`).

### Supporting commit

**`a5a3a7bbc61203398ecc1d5b52c76214f5672776`** — *"LPOS: option FIRST renamed RANK."* (antirez, 2020‑06‑24).

This commit is an ancestor of the current `HEAD`, and its message is exactly the answer. From its diff of `src/t_list.c`:

```diff
-/* LPOS key element [FIRST rank] [COUNT num-matches] [MAXLEN len]
+/* LPOS key element [RANK rank] [COUNT num-matches] [MAXLEN len]
  *
- * FIRST "rank" is the position of the match, so if it is 1, the first match
+ * The "rank" is the position of the match, so if it is 1, the first match
...
-        if (!strcasecmp(opt,"FIRST") && moreargs) {
+        if (!strcasecmp(opt,"RANK") && moreargs) {
...
-                addReplyError(c,"FIRST can't be zero: use 1 to start from "
+                addReplyError(c,"RANK can't be zero: use 1 to start from "
```

The same commit rewrote the tests from `LPOS mylist c FIRST 1` to `LPOS mylist c RANK 1` etc., confirming the user-visible option name changed.

### Why your memory is correct

The `FIRST` spelling only ever existed during the brief development window in June 2020:
- `ca58198` (2020‑06‑12, "help.h updated.") still documented `key element [FIRST rank] ...`.
- `a5a3a7b` (2020‑06‑24) renamed it to `RANK` before the command was publicly released (LPOS shipped in Redis 6.0.6 / 6.2.0). So early internal examples/tests used `FIRST`, but no released version did.

No files were modified.
